domain_symbols.complex_plane: complex numbers and planar complex domains

rules.name: Modulus-conjugate identity
preconditions: z is a complex number
rules.operation: Rewrite squared modulus as the product of a complex number with its conjugate.
examples: For z = a + bi, the identity gives |z|^2 = a^2 + b^2
counterexamples: Replacing |z|^2 by z^2 is invalid in general

rules.name: Euler formula
rules.input_form: e^(i theta)
preconditions: theta is real-valued in the standard formula
rules.operation: Convert a unit-circle complex exponential into trigonometric form.
examples: Euler's formula converts exponential oscillation into trigonometric form
counterexamples: Dropping the imaginary unit from the exponent changes the rule and is invalid

rules.name: Cauchy-Riemann seed
rules.input_form: f = u + iv holomorphic with differentiable components
preconditions: The component functions are differentiable as required
rules.operation: Use the Cauchy-Riemann equations as a standard holomorphicity test under smoothness assumptions.
examples: Verifying the Cauchy-Riemann equations is a standard holomorphicity check in smooth settings
counterexamples: Satisfying the equations without the needed regularity hypotheses is insufficient in general

rules.name: Contour integral linearity
rules.input_form: integral_gamma (af + bg) dz
rules.output_form: a integral_gamma f dz + b integral_gamma g dz
preconditions: The contour integrals involved are well-defined
rules.operation: Distribute contour integration over linear combinations of integrands.
examples: Contour integration distributes over linear combinations of integrands
counterexamples: Treating contour integration as multiplicative over sums is invalid

rules.name: Cauchy integral theorem seed
rules.input_form: closed contour integral of a holomorphic function
preconditions: The function is holomorphic on the relevant simply connected region containing the contour
rules.operation: Use holomorphicity to conclude vanishing of closed contour integrals under the standard theorem hypotheses.
examples: Holomorphicity on a disk yields vanishing closed-loop integrals in that disk
counterexamples: Applying the theorem across singularities is invalid

rules.name: Residue theorem seed
rules.input_form: closed contour integral around isolated singularities
rules.output_form: 2 pi i times sum of enclosed residues
preconditions: The contour and singularity hypotheses of the residue theorem hold
rules.operation: Reduce contour integrals to enclosed residue data under the standard theorem hypotheses.
examples: Residues convert certain complex contour integrals into local singular data
counterexamples: Summing residues outside the contour is invalid

rules.name: Cauchy integral formula seed
rules.input_form: holomorphic function and interior evaluation point
preconditions: The standard contour and holomorphicity hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Recover interior values of a holomorphic function from contour data.
examples: Cauchy integral formulas convert boundary integral data into interior function values
counterexamples: Applying the formula when the evaluation point lies on or outside the admissible contour is invalid

rules.name: Liouville theorem seed
rules.input_form: bounded entire function
preconditions: The function is entire and bounded on the whole complex plane
rules.operation: Collapse bounded entire holomorphic functions to constants.
examples: Bounded holomorphicity on the whole complex plane collapses the function to a constant
counterexamples: Boundedness on only a local region is insufficient

rules.name: Maximum modulus principle seed
rules.input_form: nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected domain
rules.output_form: no strict interior maximum of modulus
preconditions: The domain is connected and the function is holomorphic
rules.operation: Forbid strict interior modulus maxima for nonconstant holomorphic functions.
examples: Interior modulus maxima force holomorphic functions to be locally constant in the standard theorem setting
counterexamples: Applying the principle to nonholomorphic functions is invalid

rules.name: Laurent series seed
rules.input_form: holomorphic function on an annulus
preconditions: The function is holomorphic on the working annulus
rules.operation: Expand an annular holomorphic function into positive and negative complex powers.
examples: Isolated singular behavior is encoded by negative Laurent coefficients
counterexamples: Replacing annular validity by arbitrary disconnected domains is invalid

rules.name: Isolated singularity classification seed
rules.input_form: isolated singularity and Laurent expansion
preconditions: An isolated singularity and its Laurent expansion are under consideration
rules.operation: Classify isolated singularities by the negative-power structure of the Laurent series.
examples: Finitely many negative powers correspond to a pole and no negative powers correspond to a removable singularity
counterexamples: Declaring every isolated singularity a pole is invalid

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion

examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings

common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions
